questions.prompt: Which task is the best fit for plan mode?
options: Add error handling to all API routes
Look up what a library function does
questions.explanation: A change that touches many files and is easy to get wrong is worth reading a plan for before anything runs. Options A and B are small, local, and reversible, so planning is overhead with no payoff. Option D is a question, not a change — no edits means nothing to plan.

questions.prompt: In plan mode, Claude Code reads files but will not edit them without your say-so. What is plan mode?
options: A smarter model that thinks harder
A permission context — a sandbox over tools where reads are allowed and edits or side-effecting commands need your approval
An offline mode with no network
A read-only copy of your project on disk
questions.explanation: Plan mode changes which verbs are allowed for the same model, so it is a permission context, not a different brain. Option A is the tempting misconception the reframe names: it is not a smarter mode. Option C confuses sandboxing tools with cutting the network. Option D confuses a sandbox over actions with a copy of the files.

questions.prompt: You approve a plan, it executes, and then it takes a step the plan never listed. What is the correct response?
options: Push back: that step was outside the approved plan; approval is the gate, not a blank cheque
Rewind is impossible once a plan runs
questions.explanation: The approved plan is what you agreed to, so a step outside it is a real deviation worth flagging. Option A is tempting when the extra step looks harmless, but it changes the contract you approved. Option C approves something already running. Option D is false — checkpoints and rewind are the subject of the next lesson.

questions.prompt: You are unsure whether to enter plan mode for a task. What is the better default, and why?
options: Skip it — plan mode wastes tokens
Go in — plan mode is cheap, and a wrong plan costs a rewrite while a wrong action costs a revert
Only use it when you are in production
Plan mode is required for any edit touching more than one file
questions.explanation: Switching in and out is cheap, and the cost framing favours a wrong plan over a wrong action, so when unsure the answer is to go in. Option A misreads planning as expensive. Option C invents an environment rule. Option D states a hard requirement where the lesson gives a judgement call.
